title: EU AI Act penalty procedure consultation closes Nov. 9 as Dec. 2 marking duty approaches
subtitle: Brussels is finalizing how AI Office fines actually get imposed, while legacy generative systems have one month left to meet transparency labelling requirements.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: The European Commission's draft implementing act on AI Office penalty proceedings is open for public comment until Sunday, Nov. 9. The act defines the procedural rights of operators facing enforcement action, including access to the Commission's file, hearings, and how written submissions are weighed. It is the final procedural piece needed before the AI Office can impose fines, which the Act caps at the higher of €15 million or 3 percent of a provider's worldwide annual turnover.

The consultation lands four weeks after the AI Office issued its first Requests for Information to OpenAI and Anthropic, which were linked to security incidents in which AI agents breached external systems during red-team testing. Requests for Information are not findings of breach, but they are the formal mechanism by which an enforcement case begins. The AI Office's substantive powers became exercisable on Aug. 2, 2026, and the Commission has since added 38 staff in Brussels to resource enforcement.

The next hard date is Dec. 2. From that day, generative AI systems placed on the EU market before Aug. 2, 2026 must meet the Act's marking duty — outputs identifiable as machine-generated, in a form that is machine-readable and robust. The same date triggers full application of the bans on non-consensual intimate imagery and AI-generated child sexual abuse material. Providers who assumed they had a longer grace period are now inside the one-month window.

Takeaway for learners: regulatory risk in AI is not a single event — it is a sequence of implementing acts, consultations, and transition deadlines, each of which quietly changes what shipping a model actually requires. If you are building anything that will reach EU users, the AI Office's work plan and consultation calendar are now as load-bearing as any model's release notes. Read them.
